name: Kazakhstan

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 70%, Orthodox Christian about 25%

snapshot: A new constitution, rushed to a referendum in March 2026, replaced parliament with a single chamber and restored a vice president, while handing Tokayev new powers.
culture: Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country, and nomadic culture, horses, yurts and eagle hunting, is central to national identity. Kazakh is the state language, but Russian is widely spoken, especially in cities. Astana's futuristic skyline was built from scratch as a new capital in 1997. Nauryz, the spring new year, is the biggest holiday.
society: Oil, gas and uranium have made Kazakhstan Central Asia's richest country; it is the world's biggest uranium producer. Deadly unrest in January 2022 ended Nursultan Nazarbayev's behind-the-scenes rule. The country balances between Russia, China and the West and has become a key route for trade bypassing Russia.
situation: For 29 years Kazakhstan was ruled by Nursultan Nazarbayev, who built a new capital and named it after himself. His hand-picked successor, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, broke with him after deadly riots in January 2022 and promised a "New Kazakhstan" with a stronger parliament and a single seven-year presidential term. In 2026, he rewrote the constitution again, and critics say the new one points the other way.

On 15 March, voters approved a new constitution with 87 percent support on 73 percent turnout; it took effect on 1 July (CEVRO). It replaces the two-chamber parliament with a single 145-seat chamber called the Kurultai, after the old assemblies of the steppe nomads, and restores the office of vice president, which changes the line of succession. Tokayev billed it as ending the "super-presidential" system. But the president can now appoint the security chiefs, the Constitutional Court and the election commission without Senate approval, rule by decree between sessions, and dissolve parliament if it twice rejects his nominees; a vaguely worded clause narrows protection for speech that threatens "public order" (International IDEA). The whole process, from first draft to vote, took under two months, though Tokayev had earlier suggested waiting until 2027. Days later, a journalist was put under house arrest over a Telegram post. Kazakhstan, the world's largest uranium producer, has meanwhile courted Washington, Beijing and Moscow at once.
power: A presidential republic. The president is limited to one seven-year term and dominates policy and appointments; the new Kurultai is elected by proportional representation. Opposition parties are weak and protest is tightly controlled.
holders: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, since 2019; term ends 2029.
